title: Draining an abscess or boil
what: A surgeon numbs the skin, makes a small cut, and lets the pus out. Then the wound is rinsed and bandaged.
why: When pus has built up under the skin: the boil hurts, is red, gets soft in the center, and does not open by itself.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes, then dressing changes for a few days
tell_doctor: Diabetes. Boils heal more slowly in people with diabetes

prepare.title: At home
prepare.text: Do not squeeze or pop the boil yourself, especially on the face. The pus can go deeper.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can eat. A light meal 1 to 2 hours before is best.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Loose clothes, so they do not press on the bandage.

bring: Your blood sugar test results, if you have them
steps: The doctor looks at the boil
The skin around it is cleaned with antiseptic
You get a numbing injection, and the skin goes numb
A small cut is made and the pus is let out
The pocket is rinsed. Sometimes a thin strip is left in to let it drain
feel: The numbing injection burns for a few seconds
Then you feel pressure, but not pain. If it hurts, tell the doctor
When the numbing wears off, the area will ache. Regular painkillers help, as your doctor advises
after: Dressing changes are usually daily or every other day, at the clinic or at home as instructed
Keep the bandage clean and dry
Antibiotics are not always needed. Take them only if your doctor prescribed them
The wound usually heals in 1 to 2 weeks. Sometimes a small mark stays
red_flags: Redness spreading, a red streak from the wound, fever and chills: see a doctor right away
A boil on the face with a headache, swelling near the eye, or high fever: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I squeeze a boil myself?
faq.a: No. The infection can go deeper, and on the face it can even reach the blood vessels of the head. It is better to see a surgeon.
With local numbing, usually only the injection hurts. After the procedure, the pain often gets less, because the pus no longer presses.
